summary_paragraph: A woman with T2 paraplegia and a history of neurogenic bladder and chronic pressure ulcers was admitted for a worsening stage III decubitus ulcer on her right buttock that had reopened with malodor. She developed asymptomatic hypotension requiring ICU monitoring, initially concerning for sepsis, which led to broad-spectrum antibiotics. Urine culture grew pan-sensitive Escherichia coli, and treatment was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin. She developed hyponatremia (nadir 124) due to fluid overload from IV resuscitation, managed with fluid restriction and IV furosemide, with resolution by discharge. Mild pulmonary edema was noted and improved with diuresis. The ulcer was debrided twice to promote granulation tissue, and wound care was optimized with dry gauze packing. Narcotics were discontinued due to hypotension. She stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics, iron supplementation, and home health support for wound care.
